clue.text: Got rid of piece of hi-fi, a particular horror of mine

parts.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them from a job
an amp, short for amplifier, is one unit of a hi-fi system

explanation.surface: Someone sells off part of their stereo, a thing they particularly loathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of mine' reads as 'my', but it means a coal mine: a miner dreads explosive gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the explosive methane gas in coal pits, the danger colliers fear most.

clue.text: Feel ill, following first collapse

indicators.note: first places the abbreviation ahead of the rest

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
to ail is to feel unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling sick after the first sign of a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail is to break down or give way, as a collapsing structure does.

clue.text: Maybe tied up in bonds, will it bring in easy money when old?

definitions.text: Maybe tied up in bonds, will it bring in easy money when old?

parts.words: Maybe tied up in bonds, will it bring in easy money when old?
parts.note: a cord used for binding, and the idiom 'money for old' cord meaning easy earnings

explanation.walkthrough: 'bonds' and 'easy money' suggest investments; really it is the binding cord of 'money for old' fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Rope binds prisoners, and 'money for old rope' is British for easy earnings.

clue.text: Ruin listed for crew to go in and take to pieces

indicators.note: to go in says the crew is placed inside the wrecked letters
to ruin the word listed is to wreck its letters into a new order

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: Wrecking a listed building so that workers can go in and break it apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'listed' looks like a protected building, but it is the anagram fodder; 'Ruin' makes DISTLE, which 'to go in' opens up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle is to break something down into its parts.

clue.text: Say, politely what goes into Christmas pies is important

parts.note: mince, or mincemeat, fills British Christmas mince pies
something that matters is important

explanation.surface: A remark on the importance of the filling in festive pies.
explanation.walkthrough: Mince pies are small British Christmas pastries filled with spiced dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in a restrained, tactful way is to soften one's words, the sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Jack turned into. US quarters, say, in Arab citadel

indicators.note: into says the turned sailor goes inside the money

parts.note: American quarters are coins, an example of cash

indicators.note: turned asks for the sailor's letters to be read the other way round

parts.note: a jack, like an AB (able-bodied seaman), is a sailor

explanation.surface: Directions about a sailor wandering into American lodgings inside an Arab fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives BA, which 'into' sends inside the American money; a jack is a sailor, like Jack Tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the walled fortress quarter of a North African town.

clue.text: A text is accepted in error

indicators.note: accepted says the word is goes inside the manuscript

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a text

explanation.surface: A message has been received by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or out of order.

clue.text: Where one may get trapped nerve on cheek

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the nerve above the cheek

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is slang for cheek or effrontery, as in 'brass neck'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a trapped nerve in their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped nerve' reads as a medical complaint; trapped belongs to the definition, nerve to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow point where traffic or progress is held up is a congestion point.

clue.text: Game the beaters flushed out

indicators.note: flushed out suggests the beaters' letters are driven out of place

explanation.surface: Animals hunted were driven out of cover by the beaters.
explanation.definitionFit: The hartebeest is an African antelope, hunted as big game.

clue.text: I am not acting sincerely in striking

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
someone posing is putting on an act rather than being sincere

explanation.surface: A confession of insincerity in a moment of impressiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imposing is grand and impressive, as a striking sight is.

clue.text: I may say'9 is an easy catch

definitions.meaning: someone modelling for a portrait might say 'I'm posing', the answer to 9
in cricket, a catch so simple it should never be dropped

explanation.walkthrough: The 9 refers to clue 9, read as 'I'm posing': what an artist's model would say.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait model is called this, and in cricket the word also names a chance no fielder should miss.

clue.text: Endorsement of religious rite

definitions.meaning: the Christian sacrament admitting a baptised person to full membership

explanation.definitionFit: The word means verification and also names the church sacrament by which a bishop admits members.

clue.text: Governess required one to tuck ' — into some wine

parts.note: made, as in 'made him do it', means required someone to act

indicators.note: to tuck into means one letter goes inside the wine

parts.note: Moselle is a German white wine
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A governess was obliged to slip something into the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray marks in the clue are print damage; read 'to tuck into' as one container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A French governess was traditionally addressed by this title for an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Bans others playing this instrument

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are performing in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Banning others from playing a certain instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is a tenor clarinet used by Mozart.

clue.text: Irritating fliers trek leader sent round capital

indicators.note: sent round says the leader is put around the capital

parts.note: Moses led the Israelites on their trek out of Egypt
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: Annoying insects led round a city by a leader of a trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trek leader' suggests a Star Trek captain, but it is the Biblical leader of the Exodus; 'sent round' makes him the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosquitoes are biting insects, annoying creatures that fly.

clue.text: A fight joined roughly

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: A scrap was entered into, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean approximately, as in 'about ten people'.

clue.text: Plenty of illness needing a bar-.: tier as protection

indicators.note: a fence put up as protection surrounds the illness

parts.note: a fence is a barrier
flu is a common illness

explanation.surface: Lots of sickness, so a barrier is needed to keep it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'bar-.: tier' is 'barrier'; 'as protection' means the barrier surrounds the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is wealth or abundance, a state of having lots.

clue.text: Alas, not how fairy stories are supposed 'to end

definitions.meaning: a sad interjection, as in 'sadly, it rained'

definitions.text: not how fairy stories are supposed 'to end
definitions.meaning: fairy tales end 'happily ever after', so not in that way

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means sadly, and literally the opposite of the fairy-tale 'ever after' ending.

clue.text: Set aside search in The Observ er

indicators.note: in says the search sits within the observer

parts.note: a seer is one who sees, an observer
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Someone hides a search inside a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper, but it means someone who sees; 'in' makes it the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To sequester is to isolate or put apart, as a jury is.

clue.text: Take in this Latin American

parts.note: hoc is Latin for 'this'
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Asking someone to host a person from Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin American' reads as one phrase but splits: 'this Latin' and 'American'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hocus someone is to hoax or deceive them, which is what taking them in means.

clue.text: Irresponsibly aggressive, to ready to put the squeeze on?

definitions.meaning: quick to use force without thinking

definitions.text: to ready to put the squeeze on?
definitions.meaning: read literally, too keen to squeeze a gun's trigger

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'to' is 'too'. 'squeeze' looks like extortion but means pulling a trigger.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone too eager to shoot, and so reckless or belligerent.

clue.text: It was ground extremely small, and smeared on for starters by artists

definitions.text: It was ground extremely small, and smeared on for starters by artists

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Some pigment was finely powdered and applied by painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as a verb, but the paste is literally a ground: a base layer for painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gesso is a plaster paste spread as a base layer by painters and gilders.

clue.text: Said Scrooge's partner was in the country.

indicators.note: said says the partner's name is spoken aloud

parts.note: Jacob Marley was Scrooge's dead business partner in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A claim that Scrooge's partner had lived abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the partner's name and the country sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Leader of side dropped country is hurt

indicators.note: dropped says the first letter of side is removed

parts.note: Spain is a country

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The nation is wounded after the team captain is axed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is suffering or hurt.

clue.text: Player is a bit too boisterous

indicators.note: a bit of the words says the letters are a run inside them

explanation.surface: A musician is said to be rather too rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, so is a player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Painter shortly encapsulates cold current in lake

indicators.note: encapsulates says the shortened painter wraps round what follows
shortly says the painter's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A painter captures a chilly current flowing through a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts TITIAN to TITIA; 'encapsulates' puts CAC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titicaca is the large lake on the border of Peru and Bolivia.

clue.text: In old siege, he advised soldiers on weapon emplacement

indicators.note: on means the soldiers come after the emplacement

parts.note: a nest is a sheltered gun position, as in machine-gun nest
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A military adviser in an ancient siege directs troops to a gun post.
explanation.walkthrough: The old siege is that of Troy, from Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor was the aged Greek king who counselled the Greeks at Troy.

clue.text: To finish, I'm about to get into that story of Keats

parts.note: the end is the finish

indicators.note: to get into says the turned letters go inside the next word

parts.note: yon is an old word for that, as in 'yon hill'

indicators.note: about says the letters of I'm are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone finishing a book of Keats is about to get into the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives MI, and 'to get into' places it inside the old word for 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endymion is the long poem by John Keats telling the myth of the shepherd loved by the moon.
